title: Burst crosstalk isolation experiment plan
content:
Purpose
This is a working plan for a set of experiments that isolate and quantify 'burst crosstalk' effects in our inference serving runtime. By burst crosstalk I mean transient interference between concurrently serviced request bursts that causes throughput degradation or increased tail latency beyond what single-burst runs predict. The goal is to derive measurement recipes (loadgen configs, warmstart protocol, repeatability checks) that we can use in the primary throughput harness to more reliably predict production behavior.

Scope and hypotheses
- Scope: GPU-backed transformer generation models (8k context), standard KV cache enabled, batched serving runtime. Focus on end-to-end throughput under mixed microburst and steady tail loads.
- Hypothesis 1: Short, high-concurrency bursts that arrive while nearby requests are in-flight cause kernel contention and memory-bandwidth saturation leading to 10–30% throughput loss vs isolated-burst baseline.
- Hypothesis 2: Proper warmstart (KV priming + short minibatch preconditioning) can reduce observed crosstalk variance by >50%.
- Hypothesis 3: Crosstalk magnitude is sensitive to request occupancy distribution and inter-burst spacing; not captured by simple Poisson/steady generators.

Experiment design overview
We will run three classes of experiments:
1) Isolation baseline: run a single burst in isolation (no concurrent traffic) to measure ideal burst throughput and latency distribution.
2) Crosstalk matrix: pair a target burst with a background burst (varying size and spacing) to map degradation surface.
3) Warmstart interventions: repeat classes 1 and 2 with different warmstart strategies (cold, partial priming, full priming, micro-batching preconditioning).

Load generator configurations
- Generator: local loadgen (kth-emu) with deterministic request replay.
- Request workload: 50 unique prompts sampled from our internal 8k prompt set (balanced tokens: 128/512/2048 tails).
- Burst shapes: rectangular (sustained at concurrency C for duration T), triangular ramp (ramp up/down over 2s), and Poissonized microbursts (lambda set to give mean concurrency).
- Concurrency knobs: C ∈ {8, 16, 32, 64} (per-GPU logical concurrency).
- Burst durations: T ∈ {1s, 5s, 20s}.
- Inter-burst spacing: gap ∈ {0.1s, 0.5s, 2s, 10s}.
- Background traffic: steady N qps runner set to produce average occupancy O ∈ {0.1, 0.3, 0.6} of GPU slots.
- Repeat factor: each configuration runs 10 independent trials (different request order seed).

Warmstart / priming strategies
- Cold: start with empty KV cache, no preconditioning.
- KV-only: replay the first 4 prompts once to populate KV cache for hot prefixes.
- Mini-batch preconditioning: run 30s low-QPS sustained batches at 50% target concurrency immediately before burst.
- Micro-priming: send a 1s train of small token requests to spin up relevant kernels.

Measurement windows and metrics
- Warm window: exclude first 2s of each trial to avoid startup noise unless measuring cold start explicitly.
- Measurement window: for T=1s, measure full burst; for T>1s, measure middle 60% of the burst duration.
- Primary metrics: tokens/sec (throughput), p50/p90/p99 latency (generation completion), CPU/GPU utilization, PCIe / NVLINK bandwidth samples (where available), GPU memory occupancy, kernel active times (from runtime tracing).
- Secondary metrics: model-quality proxies (top-k perplexity on generated continuations), tail errors (OOMs, timeouts, 500-level errors).

Repeatability and statistical treatment
- Each experiment run = one trial. We will run 10 trials per config. For each metric compute mean and bootstrap 95% CI across trials.
- Use pairwise comparisons (paired t-test or Wilcoxon if non-normal) between baseline and crosstalk conditions.
- Flag configurations with coefficient of variation (CoV) > 10% for deeper investigation.
- Keep RNG seeds and request ordering logged for deterministic replays; all seeds stored in the artifacts bucket.

Instrumentation & logs to collect
- Loadgen logs: request timestamps, latencies, QPS, concurrency timeline.
- Runtime traces: per-request trace id, kernel launch times, queueing times, batching decisions, KV cache hits.
- System telemetry: nvidia-smi sampled at 100ms, NVLink/PCIe counters, disk IO (if swap used).
- Prometheus/metrics sink: per-worker token rates and queue lengths exported at 100ms.
- Heap/cpu profiles if we see GC or CPU spikes.

Outlier handling and drift checks
- Define outliers as trials where baseline p99 latency > 3× median baseline p99; exclude and re-run with a different seed once.
- Use control charts (Shewhart chart) across trials to detect drift across time-of-day or infra churn.

Artifacts and reproducibility
- Each trial must produce a tarball with: loadgen config, request seed, runtime trace (ndjson), prometheus snapshot, nvidia-smi CSV, and a small run-metadata.json (timestamp, model, machine-type, kernel-versions).
- Upload artifacts to gs://redwood-bench/burst-crosstalk/<config-id>/<trial-id> with consistent naming.

Experiment schedule and prioritization
- Phase 0 (quick scan): run a small combinatorial grid (C ∈ {8,32}, T ∈ {1s,5s}, gap ∈ {0.1s,2s}) with 3 trials each to find high-impact regions. (2 working days)
- Phase 1 (matrix): run full matrix with 10 trials/config across two machine types (A100-80GB, H100-80GB). (1–2 weeks)
- Phase 2 (warmstart tunings): evaluate warmstart strategies on top 5 worst-performing matrix configs. (3–4 days)

Open questions / TODOs
- Which model sizes to include beyond our default 7B/70B split? Add 3B and 92B?
- Confirm availability of NVLink counters on test fleet (ask infra).
- Decide on automation runner: use Jenkins repro harness or k8s job runner. Jenkins currently has easier access to artifact upload.
- Produce a small dashboard template for quick triage showing throughput delta heatmap across matrix.

Notes to self
- Keep the isolation baseline well-documented; too many people compare to noisy multi-tenant baselines and miss crosstalk.
- If we see >25% degradation between isolated and paired bursts at same concurrency, consider runtime-level mitigations (batch interrupt, preemption, occupancy-aware admission control).

References
- Internal: runbooks/throughput-harness, perf/kv-cache-primer, PR#4823 for loadgen fixes.
- External reading: "Mitigating microburst interference in shared GPU clusters" (SIGOPS 2021)

If this plan looks good I'll convert the Phase 0 configs into loadgen YAMLs and kick off the scans. Comments welcome — particularly on the selection of seeds/trial counts and which metrics we must capture to prove causality.
